question: Which of the following is a discretionary power of the President of India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Dissolving the Lok Sabha without advice
Appointing the Chief Justice of India
Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority
Giving assent to a Money Bill
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Appointing a Prime Minister when no party has a clear majority

Explanation:
The President of India possesses certain discretionary powers that can be exercised without the advice of the Prime Minister. One such situation arises when no single political party secures a clear majority in the Lok Sabha. In this case, the President uses his discretion to appoint a person as Prime Minister who can form a stable government. This power is derived from Article 75(1) of the Constitution. Other options are not discretionary: dissolving the Lok Sabha requires the advice of the Prime Minister, appointing the Chief Justice of India is bound by the recommendation of the outgoing CJI, and giving assent to a Money Bill is mandatory for the President.

☛ Which Article deals with the appointment of Prime Minister? → Article 75(1)
☛ Is the President bound by cabinet advice while appointing PM? → No, in case of a hung house
☛ Who advises the President to dissolve Lok Sabha? → Prime Minister
☛ Can the President withhold assent to a Money Bill? → No, it is mandatory
question_hi: निम्नलिखित में से कौन सी भारत के राष्ट्रपति की विवेकाधीन शक्ति है? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 1)

question: After its 1971 electoral victory, Indira Gandhi’s government amended the Constitution to remove legal obstacles to abolishing which of the following privileges? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Zamindari system
Monopoly trade licenses
Privy purses of former princely rulers
Separate electorates for minorities
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Privy purses of former princely rulers

Explanation:
After a landslide victory in the 1971 general election, Prime Minister Indira Gandhi's government moved to abolish the privy purses and privileges of former princely rulers. These privileges were enshrined in Articles 291 and 362 of the Indian Constitution. However, the Supreme Court in 1971 ruled that the law abolishing privy purses was unconstitutional. In response, the government passed the 26th Constitutional Amendment (1971), which deleted Articles 291 and 362 and derecognized the princely states. This amendment removed all legal obstacles to ending the privy purses and other privileges.

☛ Privy purses were related to → Former princely rulers
☛ Which article dealt with privy purses? → Article 291
☛ Prime Minister who abolished privy purses → Indira Gandhi
☛ Articles repealed by 26th Amendment → Articles 291 and 362

question: Which of the following statements about the Gram Sabha is correct? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: It consists only of elected members of the Gram Panchayat.
It has authority to override the decisions of the Panchayat.
It meets only once every five years
It comprises all adult voters in the Panchayat area; its role is defined by state law.
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is It comprises all adult voters in the Panchayat area; its role is defined by state law.

Explanation:
The Gram Sabha is a permanent body consisting of all adult voters (18 years and above) residing in the Gram Panchayat area. It forms the foundation of the Panchayati Raj system. It does not consist only of elected members; rather, every adult citizen in the area is a member. The powers and functions of the Gram Sabha are defined by state law, which varies from state to state. It cannot override decisions of the Panchayat but can provide recommendations. The Gram Sabha must meet at least twice a year, not once every five years. Its role includes discussing plans, budgets, and social audit of Panchayat activities.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:
☛ Who are members of Gram Sabha? → All adult voters in the Panchayat area
☛ How often must Gram Sabha meet? → At least twice a year
☛ Who defines powers of Gram Sabha? → State law
☛ Gram Sabha is related to which level? → Gram Panchayat level
☛ What is a key function of Gram Sabha? → Discussing Panchayat plans and budget

question: The 25th Amendment curtailed the right to property by amending which Article of Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Article 33
Article 12
Article 13
Article 31
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 31

Explanation:
The 25th Amendment (1971) to the Indian Constitution dealt with the right to property. It amended Article 31, which originally provided protection for the right to property. The amendment allowed the state to acquire any property for public purpose, and the amount of compensation was to be determined by the Parliament, not the courts. This curtailed the right to property. Later, the 44th Amendment (1978) removed the right to property from the list of Fundamental Rights and made it a legal right under Article 300A.

Important one-liners for upcoming exams:

☛ Under which Article is the right to property currently? → Article 300A
☛ Under which Prime Minister was the 25th Amendment enacted? → Indira Gandhi
☛ Which Amendment removed the right to property as a Fundamental Right? → 44th Amendment (1978)
☛ Who determined compensation under the 25th Amendment? → Parliament

question: Which of the following types of cases is NOT generally taken up by Lok Adalats in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Murder trials
Motor accident claims
Divorce settlements
Utility bill disputes
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Murder trials

Explanation:
Lok Adalats handle compoundable and civil nature cases that are amenable to settlement. They do not take up criminal cases that are non-compoundable, such as murder, heinous offenses, or cases requiring prosecution. Murder trials are criminal offenses that fall under the jurisdiction of regular courts and cannot be settled through compromise. In contrast, motor accident claims, divorce settlements, and utility bill disputes are compoundable in nature and are often resolved in Lok Adalats. The objective of Lok Adalats is to provide speedy justice and reduce the burden on regular courts, so they only take cases where mutual consent is possible.

☛ National Lok Adalat Day → Celebrated on second Saturday of November every year

question: Which of the following is the main objective of the Right to Information Act? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: To ensure secrecy in public administration
To provide private data to media houses
To promote transparency and accountability
To prevent public access to government records
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is To promote transparency and accountability

Explanation:
The main objective of the Right to Information Act (RTI), 2005 is to promote transparency and accountability in the functioning of public authorities. It empowers citizens to access information held by government bodies, enabling them to monitor government actions and curb corruption. The Act replaces secrecy with openness and strengthens the right to information under Article 19(1)(a) of the Indian Constitution. It ensures that citizens can demand information to hold the government accountable.

पारदर्शिता और जवाबदेही को बढ़ावा देना।
सरकारी रिकॉर्ड तक सार्वजनिक पहुंच को रोकना।
solution_hi:

Explanation:

question: In Indian State governments, to whom is the State Council of Ministers collectively responsible? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: The Governor of the State
Council of States
State Legislative Assembly
Chief Justice of the concerned State
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is State Legislative Assembly

Explanation:
According to Article 164 of the Indian Constitution, the State Council of Ministers is collectively responsible to the State Legislative Assembly. This is a fundamental principle of the parliamentary system of government, where the council of ministers is accountable to the lower house of the legislature. The Governor is the constitutional head, but the executive power is exercised with the aid and advice of the council of ministers. The council must maintain the confidence of the Legislative Assembly; if it loses confidence, it must resign. This provision ensures accountability of the government to the elected representatives of the people.

☛ What is the lower house of the state legislature called? → Legislative Assembly

question: Which Amendment extended the reservation of seats for SCs and STs in the legislatures for another 10 years till 2030? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: 105th Amendment
101st Amendment
104th Amendment
103rd Amendment
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is 104th Amendment

Explanation:
The 104th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2020 extended the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies for another 10 years till 2030. Earlier, the 95th Amendment (2009) had extended the reservation till 2020. This amendment amends Article 334 of the Constitution, which pertains to the reservation provisions. Additionally, the 104th Amendment also abolished the seats reserved for the Anglo-Indian community in the Lok Sabha and state assemblies. The amendment came into effect on 25 January 2020.

☛ Which community's reserved seats were abolished by the 104th Amendment? → Anglo-Indian
☛ When did the 104th Amendment come into effect? → 25 January 2020

question: The Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution relates to which of the following? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Functions of municipalities
State list subjects
Powers and responsibilities of Panchayats
Anti-defection law
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Powers and responsibilities of Panchayats

Explanation:
The Eleventh Schedule of the Indian Constitution lists the powers and responsibilities of Panchayats. It was added by the 73rd Constitutional Amendment Act of 1992, which gave constitutional status to the Panchayati Raj system. It contains 29 subjects including agriculture, education, health, rural housing, drinking water, etc. The aim is to strengthen rural local self-government. In contrast, the Twelfth Schedule relates to municipalities, the State List is in the Seventh Schedule, and the Anti-defection law is in the Tenth Schedule.

☛ Which amendment added the Eleventh Schedule? → 73rd Amendment (1992)
☛ Which articles deal with Panchayati Raj? → Articles 243–243O

☛ What does the Tenth Schedule relate to? → Anti-defection law

question: Overseas Citizen of India (OCI) holders are: (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (12/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Persons entitled to hold constitutional posts
Indian citizens with voting rights
Dual citizens of India and another country
Foreign nationals with special privileges
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Foreign nationals with special privileges

Explanation:
The Indian Constitution does not permit dual citizenship. OCI (Overseas Citizen of India) is a permanent residency visa that grants foreign nationals of Indian origin special privileges such as living and working in India, but they cannot vote or hold constitutional posts. OCI holders are not citizens of India; they are foreign nationals with special rights. They enjoy benefits like multiple-entry lifelong visa, economic and educational parity with Indian citizens, but are excluded from political rights. This status is distinct from Indian citizenship and is governed by the Citizenship Act, 1955.

☛ Which country's citizens can apply for OCI? → Any country except Pakistan and Bangladesh
☛ Can OCI holders vote in India? → No
☛ Can OCI holders hold constitutional posts? → No
☛ What is the validity of an OCI card? → Lifetime
☛ Is dual citizenship allowed in India? → No

question: Which act gave statutory status to the Central Vigilance Commission (CVC)?  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 1964
The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003
Prevention of Corruption Act, 1988
Lokpal Act, 2013
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is The Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003

Explanation:
The Central Vigilance Commission (CVC) was established in 1964 by a government resolution, but it was granted statutory status through the Central Vigilance Commission Act, 2003. This act made CVC a statutory body responsible for advising and guiding central government agencies in corruption prevention. It was formed on the recommendation of the Santhanam Committee on corruption. The CVC is an independent body whose chairman and members are appointed by the President. It has the power to direct the CBI in investigation of corruption cases under the Prevention of Corruption Act.

question: Which Article of the Constitution deals with the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes in the Lok Sabha? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: Article 332
Article 331
Article 334
Article 330
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 330

Explanation:
Article 330 of the Indian Constitution provides for the reservation of seats for Scheduled Castes (SCs) and Scheduled Tribes (STs) in the Lok Sabha. This reservation was originally for 10 years but has been extended periodically through amendments. Article 332 deals with reservation in state legislative assemblies, Article 331 provides for nomination of Anglo-Indian members by the President, and Article 334 relates to the expiration of reservation provisions. Thus, Article 330 is the core provision for SC/ST reservation in the Lok Sabha.

question: According to Article 79 of the Indian Constitution, the Parliament of India consists of:  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)
options: only Lok Sabha and Rajya Sabha
Prime Minister, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha
President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha
President, Vice President, and Prime Minister
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha

Explanation:
Article 79 of the Indian Constitution states that the Parliament of India consists of three components: the President, Lok Sabha, and Rajya Sabha. The President is an integral part of Parliament, though not a member of either house. He summons, prorogues, and dissolves Parliament. Lok Sabha is the lower house, directly elected by the people, while Rajya Sabha is the upper house, indirectly elected. Thus, option 3 is correct. Other options are incorrect as the Prime Minister or Vice President are not parts of Parliament as per Article 79.

question: Special provisions for certain states are covered under which Part of the Indian Constitution? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 1)

Part XX
Part XXI
solution:

Explanation:
Part XXI (Articles 369 to 392) of the Indian Constitution deals with special provisions for certain states. This part includes Article 370 (special status for Jammu & Kashmir, now abrogated), and Articles 371 to 371-J which provide special provisions for states like Maharashtra, Gujarat, Nagaland, Assam, Manipur, Andhra Pradesh, Telangana, Sikkim, Mizoram, Arunachal Pradesh, Goa, and Karnataka. question: Which of the following is NOT an instrument of parliamentary control over the executive in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 2)

question: The President of India is also the Supreme Commander of which force in India? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: Intelligence Agencies
Armed Forces
Border Security Force
Police Forces
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Armed Forces

Explanation:
As per Article 53(2) of the Indian Constitution, the President of India is the Supreme Commander of the Armed Forces, which includes the Army, Navy, and Air Force. This provision ensures civilian supremacy over the military. While the President holds the highest command authority, the actual administrative control is exercised by the Central Council of Ministers headed by the Prime Minister. The President can declare war or conclude peace, but only on the advice of the Council of Ministers. This system maintains democratic control and balance of military power. The President also appoints the chiefs of the three services. However, the President's role is largely ceremonial in this context, as real executive power lies with the elected government.

question: Which Act provided separate legislative subjects for the Centre and Provinces with three distinct lists? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 2)

Government of India Act 1919
Government of India Act 1935
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Government of India Act 1935

Explanation:
The Government of India Act 1935 divided legislative subjects between the Centre and Provinces through three distinct lists: Federal List, Provincial List, and Concurrent List. This act is notable for introducing provincial autonomy in India. It gave the Centre exclusive powers over the Federal List, provinces over the Provincial List, and both shared the Concurrent List. The Federal List included defense, foreign affairs, currency; the Provincial List included education, health, agriculture; and the Concurrent List included criminal procedure, labor welfare, etc. This act was a crucial step in India's constitutional development under British rule.

question: The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution is related to the:  (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 2)
options: distribution of seats in the Lok Sabha
disqualification on grounds of defection
recognition of languages
protection of land reform laws
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is disqualification on grounds of defection

Explanation:
The Tenth Schedule of the Indian Constitution, also known as the 'Anti-Defection Law', deals with the disqualification of members of Parliament and state legislatures on grounds of defection. It was added by the 52nd Amendment Act in 1985. The aim is to prevent political instability by discouraging elected representatives from switching parties. According to the Tenth Schedule, a member is disqualified if they voluntarily give up membership of their party or vote against party instructions. However, there are exceptions for party mergers. This schedule applies to both Lok Sabha and state legislative assemblies. The presiding officer of the house (Speaker/Chairman) makes the final decision on disqualification, subject to judicial review.

question: Which Article of the Constitution states, 'no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law'? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 3)
options: Article 111
Article 2
Article 300A
Article 368
solution:
Solution: Correct Answer is Article 300A

Explanation:
Article 300A of the Indian Constitution states that "no person shall be deprived of his property save by authority of law". This article was added by the 44th Amendment Act, 1978. Previously, the right to property was a fundamental right under Article 31, but the 44th Amendment removed it and made it a constitutional/legal right. Under Article 300A, the government can only take away a person's property if it is authorized by law and due process is followed. This article is placed in Part XII (Finance, Property, Contracts and Suits) under Chapter IV. It ensures that property rights are protected from arbitrary executive action.

question_hi: संविधान के किस अनुच्छेद में कहा गया है कि, 'कानून के प्राधिकार के बिना किसी भी व्यक्ति को उसकी संपत्ति से वंचित नहीं किया जाएगा'? (RRB NTPC (UG) CBT-I (13/08/2025) Shift 3)
